subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw introduce an operator-controlled way to retain custom headers such as `x-api-key` across cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and if yes must it be scoped by destination origin rather than a global header list?
rationale: The requested behavior changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public security config, so automation cannot choose the trust model or acceptable guardrails.

options.title: Design a scoped operator policy
options.body: Allow custom header retention only with explicit header validation, target-origin scoping, docs, and tests that prove the default remains strict.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and continue dropping custom credential-like headers on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add a global extension list
options.body: Implement the requested header-only config shape, accepting the higher risk that any allowed header can be replayed to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Allow custom header retention only with explicit header validation, target-origin scoping, docs, and tests that prove the default remains strict.

likelyOwner.reason: The current strict behavior traces to this security-hardening work, and the open question is whether to loosen that trust boundary.
